Definition: from G2095 and a derivative of a presumed compound of G4012 and G2476; well standing around, i.e. (a competitor) thwarting (a racer) in every direction (figuratively, of sin in genitive case):--which doth so easily beset.
BiblicalUsage: euperístatos is the word for which doth so easily beset. In Hebrews 12:1, the text says "let us lay aside every weight."
TheologicalSignificance: Out of euperístatos I do not force more than it gives: which doth so easily beset.
